openetR

openetR is a small R client for the OpenET raster API. Use it to retrieve evapotranspiration time series for a point or polygon and to inspect the metadata for an OpenET raster collection. Responses that contain rows are returned as tibbles, ready for analysis in R.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

pak::pak("ConnorB/openetR")

To install from a local checkout, use pak::pak(".").

Quick start

Create an API key in the OpenET account dashboard, then store it outside your source code:

Sys.setenv(OPENET_API_KEY = "your-api-key")
library(openetR)

openet_point_timeseries(
  longitude = -121.36322,
  latitude = 38.87626,
  start = "2020-01-01",
  end = "2020-12-31",
  interval = "monthly"
)

The package reads OPENET_API_KEY for every request. You can instead supply a key argument when credentials are managed outside the environment. Never commit an API key to a script or repository.

Choose a workflow

Task Function Geometry
Retrieve ET at one location openet_point_timeseries() longitude, latitude
Summarize ET over an area openet_polygon_timeseries() Alternating longitude/latitude pairs
Inspect a collection openet_metadata() A point or polygon

For an area query, provide alternating longitude/latitude coordinates:

openet_polygon_timeseries(
  geometry = c(-121.00747, 44.24420, -121.00747, 44.24742,
               -121.00295, 44.24742, -121.00295, 44.24422),
  start = "2021-01-01",
  end = "2021-12-31"
)

Coordinates must use WGS84 (EPSG:4326). openetR validates coordinate bounds, date order, and request options locally before making an API request.

Learn more

The package site contains a getting-started guide and a polygon workflow. OpenET limits daily point and polygon requests to ten years. Consult the OpenET API documentation for supported models, variables, quota limits, and collection details.

Contributing

Bug reports and feature requests are welcome at GitHub Issues. To work on a local checkout, run devtools::test() before submitting a change.
